question: How much will Crude Oil Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 21 - Oct 2)

calls.reasoning: Reference class anchors near zero, but this is a fat-tailed regime, not an average one: WTI is mid-shock (Hormuz ~closed, Saudi East-West pipeline attacked Sep 10, prompt ~$99.67 vs long-dated ~$60), so the spread's dispersion dominates its location. Two identifiable asymmetries pull the median slightly negative: the CL Oct contract expires Sep 22 INSIDE the window with a ~4.6% Oct/Nov backwardation gap (a ~40% chance the resolution series books that gap as a loss), and supply restoration is in motion (Saudi targeting half of East-West capacity within days, full in ~6 weeks; shuttle workarounds around Hormuz; three straight down sessions off the $106 high). Offsetting: if the series already rolled to Nov, steep backwardation gives ~+1.2% roll-up carry over 10 days, and the equity leg is itself weak (4th straight weekly loss, Fed hiking into 5%+ 10-year yields), which lifts the spread. Both tails are concrete and roughly balanced in the ensemble of analyst views (Rystad >$140 vs Goldman $85 Brent), with the negative oil-equity correlation widening rather than damping the spread. No prediction market prices this contract at any venue I could check, so no crowd anchor was used. Evidence on direction is genuinely two-sided, so I stay close to the base rate and put the work into the width.

calls.reconciliation: Three disputes mattered. (1) FACTUAL, settled: the conflicting Sep 18 WTI quotes ($95.59 Yahoo, $99.67 TradingEconomics CFD, ~$102.8 Blockonomi) are one backwardated curve read at different points - Oct ~$101.3 vs Nov ~$96.6 - with Run 2's 'Oct-26 contract' actually being November; Blockonomi's intraday surge claim contradicts three independent reports of a third straight decline and is treated as unverified. None of this changes a return question. (2) FACTUAL, partly settled and the reason my median sits above all three runs: every run applied a structural negative tilt for a front-month roll inside the window, but their own evidence (Yahoo and Barchart at ~$96 on Sep 18; InvestingLive reporting the displayed $101->$96 step that day) indicates the roll to CLX26 largely PRECEDED the Sep 21 window open. With the criteria field empty the series is unnamed, so some at-expiry-roll risk on Sep 22 survives and the tilt stays negative - just smaller, hence -1.0 rather than -1.5/-2.5. (3) JUDGMENT/computational, settled by redoing the arithmetic: OVX ~60 and VIX ~16 with negative correlation give a spread SD near 13.3 and a Gaussian 10-90 of ~34 (Run 3), but implied vol overstates realized and fat tails narrow the 10-90/SD ratio, so 31 - between Runs 1/2 and Run 3 because that is where the computation lands, not as a compromise. Also settled: the ceasefire/diplomacy state Run 2 could not confirm - Run 3's account (Apr 8 ceasefire collapsed Jul 8, no round scheduled, Hormuz shut since ~Jul 30) is consistent with the shipping-transit data all runs cite, so no in-window de-escalation catalyst is scheduled, thinning the left tail slightly. Unsettleable here: the exact resolution instrument and roll convention; I let that uncertainty live in the width rather than resolving it by fiat. Escape masses kept near the runs' consensus (0.05/0.06) since both mechanisms have each been realized once in the last ten weeks. No market prices this spread at any venue the runs could check and I retrieved nothing this run, so no crowd blend.
